locations.text: On July 6, 2013, gunmen attacked a secondary school in Mamudo, killing dozens of students. The place mattered because a rural school became one of the starkest symbols of violence against education in northeastern Nigeria. Mamudo makes the date feel intimate and devastating.

locations.name: Saïo
locations.text: On July 6, 1941, the Italian garrison at Saïo surrendered after a long East African campaign. The place mattered because an isolated stronghold marked the exhaustion of Italy's imperial position in the region. Saïo makes a global war feel resolved in a remote upland town.

locations.name: Wagram
locations.text: On July 6, 1809, Napoleon defeated Archduke Charles at Wagram in one of the largest battles of the Napoleonic Wars. The plain mattered because it became the stage for a vast, exhausting confrontation that restored French dominance after earlier setbacks. Wagram makes scale itself part of the story.

locations.name: Algeciras
locations.text: On July 6, 1801, a British squadron failed to destroy a French force at Algeciras before it could join Spanish allies. The harbor mattered because control of the Strait of Gibraltar linked local naval maneuvers to continental strategy. Algeciras makes maritime history feel tightly constrained by geography.

locations.name: Pamplona
locations.text: July 6 marks the opening of San Fermín in Pamplona, when the city pivots into one of Europe's most famous annual festivals. The place matters because its streets have become globally recognizable through ritual, spectacle, and risk. Pamplona makes celebration feel spatially choreographed.

locations.name: Brijuni
locations.text: On July 7, 1991, the Brioni Agreement helped end Slovenia's Ten-Day War and paused the breakup of Yugoslavia for a moment. The islands mattered because a resort landscape briefly hosted one of the key diplomatic pivots of the post-Yugoslav transition. Brijuni makes negotiation feel oddly serene and historically heavy at once.

locations.name: Olympiastadion
locations.text: On July 7, 1974, West Germany beat the Netherlands in the World Cup final at Munich's Olympiastadion. The stadium mattered because it became the container for one of football's most symbolically loaded finals. Olympiastadion makes sport feel like national narrative in real time.

locations.name: Dunkirk
locations.text: On July 7, 1800, British forces raided Dunkirk's anchorage during the War of the Second Coalition. The port mattered because it kept reappearing in European wars as a stubbornly strategic edge between channel and continent. Dunkirk makes recurring military relevance feel geographical rather than accidental.

locations.name: Hubbardton
locations.text: On July 7, 1777, British forces caught retreating Americans at Hubbardton, producing the only Revolutionary War battle fought in what is now Vermont. The place mattered because a rear-guard action there complicated a larger withdrawal from Ticonderoga. Hubbardton makes retreat feel stubborn and local.

locations.name: Redeswire
locations.text: On July 7, 1575, a frontier dispute triggered the Raid of the Redeswire on the Anglo-Scottish border. The pass mattered because border law and border violence could collapse into each other with almost no warning. Redeswire makes early modern diplomacy feel physically rough.

locations.name: Varna Airport
locations.text: On July 8, 2014, Lars Mittank disappeared after being filmed leaving Varna Airport, turning the terminal into the center of an internet-age mystery. The place mattered because surveillance footage made a mundane transit space endlessly rewatchable. Varna Airport makes absence feel strangely documented.

locations.name: Mineirão
locations.text: On July 8, 2014, Germany defeated Brazil 7-1 at the Mineirão in one of football's most shocking results. The stadium mattered because it transformed from home-stage expectation into a theater of collective disbelief. Mineirão makes sporting humiliation feel architectural.

locations.name: Port Sudan
locations.text: On July 8, 2003, Sudan Airways Flight 139 crashed near Port Sudan during an attempted emergency landing. The city mattered because its Red Sea gateway became associated with one of Sudan's deadliest aviation disasters. Port Sudan makes an infrastructural hub feel suddenly precarious.

locations.name: 100 Mile House
locations.text: On July 8, 1965, Canadian Pacific Air Lines Flight 21 was destroyed by a bomb near 100 Mile House in British Columbia. The place mattered because a small interior community became tied to one of Canada's most notorious air crimes. 100 Mile House makes remoteness feel forensic.

locations.name: Poltava
locations.text: On July 8, 1709, Russian forces defeated Sweden at the Battle of Poltava, decisively altering the balance of power in northern Europe. The city mattered because one battlefield there marked the collapse of Sweden's great-power moment. Poltava makes geopolitical turnover feel sudden and irreversible.

locations.name: Navaly
locations.text: On July 9, 1995, a church in Navaly was bombed during the Sri Lankan civil war after civilians had been urged to shelter there. The place mattered because a site of presumed refuge became the scene of mass death. Navaly makes the cruelty of war feel concentrated and unbearable.

locations.name: Buckingham Palace
locations.text: On July 9, 1982, Michael Fagan entered Queen Elizabeth II's bedroom in Buckingham Palace, exposing a startling breach in royal security. The palace mattered because one of the world's most guarded symbolic residences was suddenly shown to be permeable. Buckingham Palace makes monarchy feel oddly vulnerable.

locations.name: Nintendo
locations.text: On July 9, 1981, Nintendo released Donkey Kong, introducing Mario to the world. The company mattered because its Kyoto base became one of the key launch points for modern video-game culture. Nintendo makes a corporate address feel like creative infrastructure.

locations.name: Ferus Gallery
locations.text: On July 9, 1962, Andy Warhol's Campbell's Soup Cans exhibition opened at the Ferus Gallery in Los Angeles. The gallery mattered because a relatively small art space became the setting for one of pop art's most durable shocks. Ferus Gallery makes aesthetic turning points feel room-sized.

locations.name: Beirut
locations.text: On July 9, 551, a major earthquake devastated Beirut and the surrounding coast of Phoenice. The city mattered because it was a major center of Roman urban life, law, and commerce in the eastern Mediterranean. Beirut makes deep history feel seismically fragile.

locations.name: Tham Luang Nang Non
locations.text: On July 10, 2018, the last members of a trapped youth football team and their coach were rescued from Tham Luang Nang Non. The cave mattered because it turned a local emergency into an intensely followed global operation. Tham Luang Nang Non makes rescue feel geological, technical, and collective.

locations.name: Nago
locations.text: On July 10, 1945, three U.S. Marines who had repeatedly assaulted local women near Nago were killed by residents and hidden in a cave, in an incident suppressed for decades. The place mattered because it preserves a deeply uncomfortable history of occupation, violence, and local retaliation. Nago makes the war's aftermath feel morally jagged.

locations.name: Jedwabne
locations.text: On July 10, 1941, Jewish residents of Jedwabne were murdered in one of the most disputed and painful atrocities of wartime Poland. The town mattered because it forced later generations to confront questions of collaboration, memory, and national narrative. Jedwabne makes historical reckoning intensely local.

locations.name: Vellore Fort
locations.text: On July 10, 1806, Indian sepoys mutinied at Vellore Fort in one of the earliest major military rebellions against the East India Company. The fort mattered because the uprising anticipated many of the tensions that would erupt more widely in 1857. Vellore Fort makes imperial control feel brittle behind stone walls.

locations.name: Portobelo
locations.text: On July 10, 1668, Henry Morgan's forces landed at Portobelo in an assault that helped make the town famous across the Caribbean world. The place mattered because its fortifications were central to Spain's treasure routes and to the mythology of piracy. Portobelo makes imperial wealth feel vulnerable at the shoreline.

locations.name: Srebrenica
locations.text: July 11 is marked internationally in memory of the Srebrenica genocide after the fall of the enclave in 1995. Srebrenica matters because the town became one of the clearest and most painful symbols of the Bosnian war's worst atrocity.

locations.name: Jeddah
locations.text: On July 11, 1991, Nigeria Airways Flight 2120 departed Jeddah before crashing after takeoff, killing everyone aboard. Jeddah matters because one of the deadliest aviation disasters tied to the hajj travel corridor began there.

locations.name: Kortrijk
locations.text: On July 11, 1302, the Battle of the Golden Spurs was fought near Kortrijk, becoming one of medieval Flanders's defining victories. Kortrijk matters because the battle stayed central to Flemish historical identity long after the armor was cleared away.

locations.name: Evangelos Florakis Naval Base
locations.text: On July 11, 2011, a blast at Evangelos Florakis Naval Base killed 13 people and triggered one of the worst peacetime crises in modern Cyprus. The base matters because a military storage failure there rippled into national outrage, political fallout, and a major power shortage.

locations.name: Assembly Rooms, Belfast
locations.text: On July 11, 1792, the Belfast Harp Festival opened at the Assembly Rooms and became a landmark moment in preserving Irish musical traditions. The venue matters because a local gathering there helped shape later ideas of cultural memory and revival.

locations.name: Saint Basil's Cathedral
locations.text: On July 12, 1561, Saint Basil's Cathedral was consecrated in Moscow. The cathedral matters because its silhouette became one of the most recognizable architectural emblems of Russian power and religion.

locations.name: Lod
locations.text: On July 12, 1948, expulsions from Lydda, now Lod, became one of the most disputed episodes of the 1948 Arab-Israeli war. Lod matters because the city's story remains central to arguments about displacement, memory, and statehood.

locations.name: Vidin
locations.text: On July 12, 1396, the siege of Vidin began during the Ottoman expansion into the Balkans. Vidin matters because frontier strongholds like it marked the slow political transformation of southeastern Europe.

locations.name: Woodstock, New Brunswick
locations.text: On July 12, 1847, riots broke out in Woodstock amid sectarian tensions in New Brunswick. Woodstock matters because a small town briefly exposed how imported imperial conflicts could harden into local violence.

locations.name: Fort Souville
locations.text: On July 12, 1916, German forces launched a major attack toward Fort Souville during the Battle of Verdun. The fort matters because holding it helped prevent the battlefield from tipping irreversibly against the French.

locations.name: Taiwan
locations.text: On July 13, 2013, Typhoon Soulik made landfall in Taiwan and caused widespread disruption. Taiwan matters because the island repeatedly turns major weather events into stories of exposure, infrastructure, and resilience.

locations.name: Dubrovnik
locations.text: On July 13, 1992, Operation Tiger ended with Croatian forces pushing the front back from Dubrovnik's hinterland. Dubrovnik matters because the city's survival became one of the most visible stakes of the Croatian war.

locations.name: Lake Piru
locations.text: On July 13, 2020, the body of actor Naya Rivera was recovered from Lake Piru after a widely followed search. Lake Piru matters because a recreation site turned into a national scene of grief and attention.

locations.name: Devizes
locations.text: On July 13, 1643, the Battle of Roundway Down was fought near Devizes during the English Civil War. Devizes matters because a town under pressure suddenly sat beside one of the war's most dramatic royalist victories.

locations.name: Durbe
locations.text: On July 13, 1260, the Battle of Durbe dealt the Teutonic Order one of its sharpest defeats. Durbe matters because a relatively small Baltic battlefield helped shift the regional balance of power.

locations.name: Matterhorn
locations.text: On July 14, 1865, the Matterhorn was first climbed, though the achievement was immediately shadowed by a fatal descent. The Matterhorn matters because mountaineering triumph and disaster arrived there together.

locations.name: Nice
locations.text: On July 14, 2016, a truck attack on the Promenade des Anglais in Nice killed dozens during Bastille Day celebrations. Nice matters because a festive national holiday there became the site of one of France's most traumatic recent attacks.

locations.name: Daejeon
locations.text: On July 14, 1950, fighting intensified around Daejeon during one of the Korean War's most important early battles. Daejeon matters because the city's fall showed how quickly the war's front could collapse southward.

locations.name: Polillo Island
locations.text: On July 14, 1948, Northwest Orient Flight 1-11 ditched off Polillo Island after an engine fire. Polillo Island matters because an otherwise peripheral island entered aviation history through a rare and dramatic sea landing.

locations.name: Delville Wood
locations.text: On July 14, 1916, the struggle for Delville Wood began as part of the Somme offensive. Delville Wood matters because the small forest became synonymous with attrition, sacrifice, and battlefield devastation.

locations.name: Manitoba
locations.text: On July 15, 1870, Manitoba entered Confederation as a new Canadian province. Manitoba matters because its creation sat at the intersection of expansion, settlement, and the Red River resistance.

locations.name: Palermo
locations.text: July 15 is the feast of Saint Rosalia, when Palermo centers one of Sicily's most important civic and religious festivals. Palermo matters because the city folds plague memory, devotion, and spectacle into one annual ritual.

locations.name: Grunwald
locations.text: On July 15, 1410, the Battle of Grunwald ended in a devastating defeat for the Teutonic Order. Grunwald matters because the field still anchors Polish and Lithuanian historical memory of a decisive medieval victory.

locations.name: Fiordland
locations.text: On July 15, 2009, a major earthquake struck the Fiordland region in New Zealand. Fiordland matters because its dramatic remoteness does not insulate it from the raw tectonic forces that shape the country.

locations.name: Fort Julien
locations.text: On July 15, 1799, the Rosetta Stone was discovered at Fort Julien during Napoleon's Egyptian campaign. Fort Julien matters because one military site accidentally opened a path to deciphering ancient Egyptian writing.

locations.name: Bihar
locations.text: On July 16, 2013, a school meal poisoning in Bihar killed children and shocked the country. Bihar matters because the tragedy turned a basic welfare program into a stark story about safety, trust, and governance.

locations.name: Luzon
locations.text: On July 16, 1990, a devastating earthquake struck Luzon and killed more than a thousand people. Luzon matters because the disaster reshaped how the Philippines thought about seismic risk, urban vulnerability, and preparedness.

locations.name: Kashiwazaki-Kariwa Nuclear Power Plant
locations.text: On July 16, 2007, an earthquake affected the Kashiwazaki-Kariwa Nuclear Power Plant and triggered serious concern about reactor safety. The plant matters because it exposed how natural hazards and nuclear infrastructure can collide.

locations.name: Arjona
locations.text: On July 16, 1232, Muhammad ibn Yusuf was proclaimed ruler in Arjona, beginning the Nasrid rise in al-Andalus. Arjona matters because a small Andalusian town briefly stood at the start of a dynasty with long regional consequences.

locations.name: Maracana Stadium
locations.text: On July 16, 1950, Uruguay stunned Brazil in the World Cup final at Maracana Stadium. The stadium matters because one result there became one of football's most enduring national traumas.

locations.name: Yekaterinburg
locations.text: On July 17, 1918, the Romanov family were executed in Yekaterinburg. Yekaterinburg matters because the city became inseparable from the violent end of imperial Russia.

locations.name: Olympia
locations.text: On July 17, 1948, the first modern Olympic torch relay for a summer Games began in Olympia before heading toward London. Olympia matters because the ancient site keeps being repurposed as a stage for modern ritual and continuity.

locations.name: Yasaka Shrine
locations.text: July 17 is the centerpiece of Kyoto's Gion Matsuri, anchored at Yasaka Shrine. The shrine matters because one of Japan's most famous festivals radiates from it through processions, ritual, and urban choreography.

locations.name: Coppermine River
locations.text: On July 17, 1771, the Bloody Falls massacre took place on the Coppermine River during Samuel Hearne's northern expedition. The river matters because an exploration route there also preserves a history of violence and encounter.

locations.name: Port Chicago Naval Magazine National Memorial
locations.text: On July 17, 1944, an explosion at Port Chicago killed 320 people and exposed racial inequities in the wartime U.S. Navy. The memorial matters because the site links disaster history directly to the struggle over military segregation.

locations.name: Treblinka extermination camp
locations.text: On July 18, 1942, gas chambers at Treblinka began operating during one of the deadliest phases of the Holocaust. Treblinka matters because the camp stands as one of the clearest place-names of industrialized murder.

locations.name: Long Island City
locations.text: On July 18, 1899, the newsboys' strike began in Long Island City before spreading more widely through New York. Long Island City matters because a localized labor dispute there became a broader fight over press distribution and child workers.

locations.name: Birgu
locations.text: On July 18, 1806, a gunpowder magazine exploded in Birgu and devastated part of the old Maltese city. Birgu matters because its dense urban fabric turned one accident into a disaster with lasting local memory.

locations.name: Burgas Airport
locations.text: On July 18, 2012, a bombing at Burgas Airport killed Israeli tourists and a Bulgarian driver. The airport matters because an ordinary arrival point became a site of international terror and diplomatic fallout.

locations.name: Hough
locations.text: On July 18, 1966, the Hough riots began in Cleveland after years of racial inequality and police tension. Hough matters because the neighborhood became a concentrated expression of urban unrest in the United States.

locations.name: Bunbury
locations.text: On July 19, 1976, a bomb damaged facilities at Bunbury Harbour in Western Australia. Bunbury matters because a port city better known for trade briefly entered national attention through political violence.

locations.name: Via D'Amelio
locations.text: On July 19, 1992, judge Paolo Borsellino was assassinated in the Via D'Amelio bombing in Palermo. The street matters because anti-mafia history in Italy is permanently tied to that one explosion.

locations.name: Kliszow
locations.text: On July 19, 1702, Swedish forces won the Battle of Kliszow during the Great Northern War. Kliszow matters because one relatively obscure field became part of a war that reordered the Baltic world.

locations.name: Fromelles
locations.text: On July 19, 1916, the Battle of Fromelles began and became one of Australia's worst days of the First World War. Fromelles matters because a small French village became a byword for futile slaughter.

locations.name: Farafra
locations.text: On July 19, 2014, militants killed soldiers in the Farafra oasis region in Egypt's Western Desert. Farafra matters because an isolated outpost there highlighted the reach of insecurity far from Cairo.

locations.name: Genoa
locations.text: On July 20, 2001, protests at the G8 summit in Genoa turned deadly with the killing of Carlo Giuliani. Genoa matters because the city became shorthand for the clash between anti-globalization protest and state force.

locations.name: Berwick-upon-Tweed
locations.text: On July 20, 1333, Berwick fell after a major siege during the Second War of Scottish Independence. Berwick-upon-Tweed matters because its border position kept making it strategically important far beyond its size.

locations.name: Bella Coola
locations.text: On July 20, 1793, Alexander Mackenzie reached the Pacific near Bella Coola, completing a transcontinental overland journey. Bella Coola matters because an inlet on the central coast briefly marked the edge of imperial geographic ambition.

locations.name: Inverkeithing
locations.text: On July 20, 1651, the Battle of Inverkeithing opened the way for Cromwellian control in Scotland. Inverkeithing matters because one Fife town became a turning point in the Wars of the Three Kingdoms.

locations.name: Suruc
locations.text: On July 20, 2015, a suicide bombing in Suruc killed young activists preparing to help rebuild Kobani. Suruc matters because the border town became a focal point of the Syrian war's spillover into Turkey.

locations.name: Crete
locations.text: On July 21, 365, a massive earthquake near Crete sent destructive tsunami waves across the eastern Mediterranean. Crete matters because one tectonic event there reverberated through a much larger ancient world.

locations.name: Belfast
locations.text: On July 21, 1972, Bloody Friday bombings struck central Belfast during the Troubles. Belfast matters because the city repeatedly compressed sectarian conflict, security policy, and civilian fear into a single urban space.

locations.name: Florence
locations.text: On July 21, 1378, the Ciompi Revolt seized control in Florence and briefly upended the city's political order. Florence matters because labor unrest there cut straight into one of medieval Europe's richest republics.

locations.name: Yuen Long
locations.text: On July 21, 2019, men in white shirts attacked commuters and protesters inside Yuen Long station and nearby streets. Yuen Long matters because the district became one of the most notorious symbols of the Hong Kong protest crisis.

locations.name: Sallum
locations.text: On July 21, 1977, clashes around Sallum helped trigger the brief Egypt-Libya War. Sallum matters because a border town there became the hinge between rhetorical hostility and actual interstate fighting.

locations.name: Hanoi
locations.text: On July 22, 1802, Gia Long took Hanoi as he consolidated rule over a unified Vietnam. Hanoi matters because control of the city kept serving as a marker of political legitimacy in Vietnamese history.

locations.name: Sarawak
locations.text: July 22 is celebrated as Sarawak Day, marking the territory's attainment of self-government in 1963. Sarawak matters because the date remains central to how the state narrates autonomy, federation, and identity.

locations.name: Beziers
locations.text: On July 22, 1209, crusaders sacked Beziers in one of the defining atrocities of the Albigensian Crusade. Beziers matters because the city's fall became shorthand for indiscriminate violence carried out in the name of orthodoxy.

locations.name: Kapustin Yar
locations.text: On July 22, 1951, Soviet dogs Dezik and Tsygan were launched from Kapustin Yar and returned alive, marking an early milestone in spaceflight biology. Kapustin Yar matters because so much Cold War experimentation began in remote testing grounds like this one.

locations.name: Aughrim
locations.text: On July 22, 1691, the Battle of Aughrim ended in a crushing Jacobite defeat. Aughrim matters because the field became one of the most decisive and deadly sites in the Williamite war in Ireland.

locations.name: Valencia, Santa Clarita
locations.text: On July 23, 1982, a helicopter crash during filming in Valencia killed actor Vic Morrow and two children. Valencia, Santa Clarita matters because one production site became central to later debates over film safety and liability.

locations.name: Lewes
locations.text: On July 23, 1958, the trial over the killing of Ruth Ellis's lover opened in Lewes after a violent seaside encounter had drawn national attention. Lewes matters because a provincial court there became part of a much larger public fascination with crime and punishment.

locations.name: Kronstadt
locations.text: On July 23, 1891, a French naval visit to Kronstadt helped signal the coming Franco-Russian alliance. Kronstadt matters because a naval base in the Gulf of Finland briefly became a stage for European realignment.

locations.name: Site of the First National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party
locations.text: On July 23, 1921, delegates met in Shanghai for the First National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party. The site matters because one modest meeting place became foundational to the political history of modern China.

locations.name: Tulia
locations.text: On July 23, 1999, mass drug arrests in Tulia began a case that later became notorious for wrongful convictions and racial bias. Tulia matters because a small Texas town turned into a national example of fabricated justice.

locations.name: Montreal
locations.text: On July 24, 1987, a cloudburst flood overwhelmed Montreal and paralyzed parts of the city. Montreal matters because a modern metropolis there was abruptly reminded how exposed infrastructure can be to extreme rain.

locations.name: Ouagadougou
locations.text: On July 24, 2014, Air Algerie Flight 5017 departed from Ouagadougou before crashing in Mali. Ouagadougou matters because a major West African hub briefly became the beginning of a tragic trans-Sahel journey.

locations.name: Shkoder
locations.text: On July 24, 1910, Ottoman forces captured Shkoder during the Albanian revolt. Shkoder matters because the city repeatedly sat at the intersection of imperial decline, rebellion, and Balkan state formation.

locations.name: Maysalun
locations.text: On July 24, 1920, French forces defeated Syrian troops at Maysalun and advanced on Damascus. Maysalun matters because the battlefield became a lasting symbol of anticolonial sacrifice in Syrian memory.

locations.name: Inverurie
locations.text: On July 24, 1411, the Battle of Harlaw was fought near Inverurie in northeastern Scotland. Inverurie matters because the encounter remained embedded in Scottish memory as a conflict over power, succession, and region.

locations.name: Osaka
locations.text: July 25 is one of the main days of Tenjin Matsuri in Osaka, among Japan's most famous urban festivals. Osaka matters because the city channels commerce, devotion, and spectacle into a celebration with deep local continuity.

locations.name: Corinth Canal
locations.text: On July 25, 1893, the Corinth Canal was formally opened after decades of engineering ambition. The canal matters because it turned an ancient geographical shortcut into a modern infrastructural statement.

locations.name: Reims Cathedral
locations.text: On July 25, 1547, Henry II of France was crowned at Reims Cathedral. The cathedral matters because so much of French royal legitimacy was ceremonially concentrated in that one building.

locations.name: Gonesse
locations.text: On July 25, 2000, Air France Flight 4590 crashed near Gonesse shortly after takeoff from Paris. Gonesse matters because the town became forever linked to the Concorde's only fatal accident.

locations.name: Knodsenburg
locations.text: On July 25, 1591, relief of the siege of Knodsenburg marked a Dutch success in the Eighty Years' War. Knodsenburg matters because small fortified points like it often carried strategic weight beyond their size.

locations.name: Vimy Memorial
locations.text: On July 26, 1936, the Canadian National Vimy Memorial was unveiled in France. The memorial matters because it transformed one battlefield into a national site of grief, sacrifice, and identity.

locations.name: Cittadella (Gozo)
locations.text: On July 26, 1551, the Cittadella on Gozo surrendered during an Ottoman raid that devastated the island. The citadel matters because its fall condensed the vulnerability of Mediterranean island societies to imperial attack.

locations.name: Stellaland
locations.text: On July 26, 1882, the Boer republic of Stellaland was established in southern Africa. Stellaland matters because ephemeral states like it reveal how fluid frontiers and authority could be during settler expansion.

locations.name: Pryazovia
locations.text: On July 26, 1778, the Russian Empire ordered the resettlement of Crimean Greeks to Pryazovia. Pryazovia matters because the region became a destination for forced demographic engineering with long historical consequences.

locations.name: Mokpo Air Base
locations.text: On July 26, 1993, Asiana Airlines Flight 733 crashed during approach to Mokpo Air Base in poor weather. The air base matters because a military-linked runway became central to one of South Korea's deadliest air disasters.

locations.name: Phoenix
locations.text: On July 27, 2007, two television news helicopters collided over Phoenix during a live police chase broadcast. Phoenix matters because the city became the backdrop for one of the most surreal media-era air disasters.

locations.name: Thessaloniki
locations.text: On July 27, 586, a major siege of Thessaloniki by the Sclaveni came to an end. Thessaloniki matters because the city kept functioning as one of the eastern Mediterranean's most resilient urban strongholds.

locations.name: Bruges
locations.text: On July 27, 1916, British captain Charles Fryatt was executed in Bruges by German authorities. Bruges matters because a city better known for its medieval calm became entangled in the harsh symbolism of wartime justice.

locations.name: El Alamein
locations.text: On July 27, 1942, the First Battle of El Alamein ended with the Axis advance checked in Egypt. El Alamein matters because the name became synonymous with one of the Second World War's crucial turning points in North Africa.

locations.name: Visby Cathedral
locations.text: On July 27, 1225, Visby Cathedral was consecrated on Gotland. The cathedral matters because it reflects how a Hanseatic trading town expressed its status through monumental religion.

locations.name: San Marino
locations.text: July 28 is celebrated as Liberation Day in San Marino, commemorating the end of Fascist rule. San Marino matters because even one of Europe's smallest states carries a sharply remembered political chronology.

locations.name: Fukuoka
locations.text: On July 28, 2001, Ian Thorpe completed his six-gold performance at the world swimming championships in Fukuoka. Fukuoka matters because the city briefly hosted one of the defining meets of modern swimming.

locations.name: Sutton Hoo
locations.text: On July 28, 1939, the famous Sutton Hoo helmet was uncovered during the excavation of the Anglo-Saxon ship burial. Sutton Hoo matters because one archaeological site there transformed understanding of early medieval England.

locations.name: Margalla Hills
locations.text: On July 28, 2010, Airblue Flight 202 crashed in the Margalla Hills during approach to Islamabad. The hills matter because a landscape beside the capital became associated with one of Pakistan's deadliest air disasters.

locations.name: Tangshan
locations.text: On July 28, 1976, the Tangshan earthquake killed vast numbers of people in one of the twentieth century's deadliest disasters. Tangshan matters because the city's name remains almost inseparable from catastrophic urban destruction.

locations.name: St Paul's Cathedral
locations.text: On July 29, 1981, the wedding of Charles and Diana took place at St Paul's Cathedral. The cathedral matters because a single ceremony there became one of the most globally watched royal spectacles of the twentieth century.

locations.name: Stirling
locations.text: On July 29, 1567, James VI of Scotland was crowned at Stirling. Stirling matters because the city and its castle long served as a compact stage for Scottish monarchy, crisis, and continuity.

locations.name: Monza
locations.text: On July 29, 1900, King Umberto I of Italy was assassinated in Monza. Monza matters because the city unexpectedly became the scene of a dramatic rupture in Italian political life.

locations.name: Klyuch
locations.text: On July 29, 1014, the Battle of Kleidion was fought near Klyuch and helped break Bulgarian resistance to Byzantium. Klyuch matters because one valley battlefield carried major consequences for medieval Balkan power.

locations.name: Neerwinden
locations.text: On July 29, 1693, the Battle of Landen was fought around Neerwinden during the Nine Years' War. Neerwinden matters because seemingly quiet Flemish villages were often pulled into Europe's dynastic wars.

locations.name: Lodz
locations.text: On July 30, 1981, hunger demonstrations in Lodz drew attention to shortages and social strain in late communist Poland. Lodz matters because an industrial city there helped make economic breakdown politically visible.

locations.name: Chihuahua City
locations.text: On July 30, 1811, Miguel Hidalgo was executed in Chihuahua City during the Mexican War of Independence. Chihuahua City matters because one northern city became part of the founding martyrdom of the Mexican nation.

locations.name: Qana
locations.text: On July 30, 2006, an airstrike near Qana killed civilians sheltering during the Lebanon war. Qana matters because the village's name had already become deeply associated with earlier wartime trauma.

locations.name: Grace-Berleur
locations.text: On July 30, 1950, police opened fire in Grace-Berleur during the crisis over King Leopold III. Grace-Berleur matters because a local confrontation there captured the intensity of Belgium's postwar royal question.

locations.name: Malin
locations.text: On July 30, 2014, a landslide buried much of the village of Malin in Maharashtra. Malin matters because the disaster turned a small settlement into a national warning about terrain, rain, and rural vulnerability.

locations.name: K2
locations.text: On July 31, 1954, climbers first reached the summit of K2, one of the world's most difficult mountains. K2 matters because success there still signifies a harsher and more dangerous mountaineering benchmark than Everest-style fame.

locations.name: Ypres
locations.text: On July 31, 1917, the Battle of Passchendaele began near Ypres. Ypres matters because the city remained one of the Western Front's most concentrated landscapes of mud, artillery, and attrition.

locations.name: Ten Thousand Buddhas Monastery
locations.text: On July 31, 2000, the Ten Thousand Buddhas Monastery fully reopened after restoration. The monastery matters because it shows how a highly recognizable religious site can become a cultural landmark beyond its devotional role.

locations.name: Claudy
locations.text: On July 31, 1972, coordinated car bombs killed civilians in Claudy during the Troubles. Claudy matters because the village shows how violence in Northern Ireland repeatedly reached places far smaller than the better-known cities.

locations.name: Medininkai
locations.text: On July 31, 1991, Lithuanian customs officials were killed at Medininkai during the violent last phase of Soviet collapse. Medininkai matters because a border post there became a stark symbol of independence achieved under pressure.
